title: Week 05 · AI Remix Lab — Same Idea, Different Reality
description: A 75-minute AI Remix Lab aligned to the planned Week 05 PowerPoint. Students experience how modality changes communication, connect the experience to the course model, watch a live remix, design for a specific audience, create two modalities, compare artifacts, evaluate polished-but-wrong outputs, and close with evidence-based reflection.

steps.label: COLD OPEN
steps.title: Which one would actually make you do something?
steps.lead: Same message: “Stop procrastinating and start the assignment.”
choices: TEXT — Future you is begging current you to start.
IMAGE — 11:58 PM. Laptop open. Upload bar at 3%.
VIDEO / MEME — POV: You remembered the assignment at 11:58.
steps.studentTask: Scan all four. Pick the version most likely to get your attention and make you act. Be ready to explain why.
steps.roomInstruction: SAME IDEA · DIFFERENT REALITY · Which version would actually make you act?
steps.visualAccent: Text → Image → Audio → Video → Human Judgment
steps.visualCaption: Do not choose the coolest format. Choose the one most likely to work on you.

runbook.openWith: Today is a lab, not a tool tour. We are going to take one idea and keep changing the form until it feels like a different experience.
runbook.whyMatters: Creates curiosity before terminology and makes modality personally relevant.
runbook.ask: Which one gets your attention? Which one actually makes you start? Are those the same answer?
runbook.pause: 15 seconds quiet scan, then quick responses
runbook.listenFor: Speed, humor, emotion, clarity, annoyance, memorability, accessibility, social context.
runbook.ifTheySay: Video is best → ask: Best for attention, understanding, remembering, or taking action?
runbook.ifQuiet: Use the RA reminder example: wall-of-text email, funny hallway poster, 10-second group-chat video.
runbook.pushFurther: What changed if the core message stayed almost the same?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: The content barely changed. The experience of receiving it did.
runbook.landHere: Modality changes what people notice, feel, understand, remember, trust, and do.
runbook.transition: Let’s make the variation in the room visible.
runbook.studentDoes: Chooses a format and explains the effect it has on them.
runbook.askNext: Are attention and effectiveness always the same thing?
runbook.watchFor: Tool-brand talk. Redirect to the form of the output.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask which format they would notice in Canvas versus a group chat.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can name at least two reasons the format changed their reaction.

steps.label: QUICK VOTE
steps.title: Pick your winner.
steps.lead: Which format would be most effective for you?
steps.studentTask: Vote quickly. Then listen for why someone made a different choice than you.
steps.roomInstruction: TEXT · IMAGE · AUDIO · VIDEO / MEME — pick one and defend WHY.
steps.visualCaption: We do not all experience the same modality the same way.

runbook.openWith: This is not about finding the class winner. I want to make human variation visible.
runbook.whyMatters: Shows that effective communication depends on audience, not a universal best format.
runbook.ask: Give me one 10-second reason for two different choices.
runbook.listenFor: Preference, context, speed, emotion, trust, ease of processing.
runbook.ifTheySay: Everyone my age prefers video → ask whether they would want scholarship instructions or an exam policy only as video.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask one TEXT voter and one VIDEO voter.
runbook.pushFurther: Would your answer change for urgent, private, complicated, or high-stakes information?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Same idea, different people, different reactions.
runbook.landHere: The best modality depends on who, what, where, and why.
runbook.transition: Now let’s name what actually changed.
runbook.studentDoes: Votes and compares reasoning across classmates.
runbook.askNext: What dimensions changed when the format changed?
runbook.ifStuck: Offer: attention, clarity, emotion, trust, effort.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students recognize there is no single winner.

steps.label: DEBRIEF
steps.title: Same idea. Different reaction. Why?
steps.lead: The message did not change much. The modality did.
steps.studentTask: Name what changed for the audience when the format changed. Select the dimensions that matter most in your examples.
steps.roomInstruction: ATTENTION · EMOTION · CLARITY · ACCESSIBILITY · TRUST · EFFORT
steps.visualCaption: It changes what becomes easy—or hard—for the audience.

runbook.openWith: Use your own language first: what changed when the format changed?
runbook.whyMatters: Builds a shared vocabulary for later comparison.
runbook.ask: Which of these changed most in our cold open?
runbook.listenFor: Attention, emotion, clarity, accessibility, trust, effort, memorability.
runbook.ifTheySay: Images are clearer → ask clearer for what kind of information?
runbook.ifQuiet: Use examples: dining-hall map vs written directions; official-looking graphic that is wrong; video without captions.
runbook.pushFurther: Can a format increase trust without increasing truth?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: A polished format can increase confidence even when the information is wrong.
runbook.landHere: Modality shapes the audience experience and can introduce new strengths and risks.
runbook.transition: Now we can define multimodal AI and reconnect it to the model we have used all semester.
runbook.studentDoes: Uses analytical vocabulary to explain format effects.
runbook.askNext: Where does multimodal AI fit into our course model?
runbook.ifStuck: Ask what became easier and what became harder.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can name a gain and tradeoff created by modality.

steps.label: CORE MODEL
steps.title: The framework we keep coming back to.
steps.lead: INPUT / DATA → MODEL / TOOL → OUTPUT → HUMAN DECISION
steps.studentTask: Follow the model with one example. Identify where the modality changes and where human responsibility remains.
steps.roomInstruction: INPUT / DATA → MODEL / TOOL → OUTPUT → HUMAN DECISION
steps.visualAccent: The modality can change. The human decision does not disappear.
steps.visualCaption: Multimodal AI can interpret or generate across text, images, audio, video, and mixed forms.

runbook.openWith: Multimodal AI can interpret or generate across different kinds of information—text, images, audio, video, or combinations of them.
runbook.whyMatters: Connects Week 05 to the durable course framework rather than a list of tools.
runbook.ask: If I upload a photo and AI answers in text, how many modalities are involved?
runbook.listenFor: Input modality, model/tool, output modality, human evaluation and action.
runbook.ifTheySay: The AI owns the decision → return to the human decision box.
runbook.ifQuiet: Use the campus event poster example: date/location/audience → AI tool → polished poster → human checks date, room, tone, accessibility, whether to post.
runbook.pushFurther: Which box carries responsibility for consequences?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: AI can change the form of the work. It does not remove responsibility for the decision.
runbook.landHere: Multimodal AI expands inputs and outputs; human judgment remains part of the system.
runbook.transition: Let’s watch one idea move through different modalities.
runbook.studentDoes: Maps a multimodal example to the recurring course model.
runbook.askNext: What do we gain—and lose—when the output changes form?
runbook.watchFor: Confusing multimodal with only image generation.
runbook.ifStuck: Use photo→text, voice note→study outline, brief→storyboard.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can explain multimodal AI in plain language and locate human judgment.

steps.label: LIVE REMIX
steps.title: Watch the idea change.
steps.lead: “Explain why multifactor authentication matters to someone who is tired of hearing about cybersecurity.”
steps.studentTask: For each remix, track three things: What improved? What got worse? What would you verify?
steps.roomInstruction: WHAT IMPROVED? · WHAT GOT WORSE? · WHAT WOULD YOU VERIFY?
steps.visualAccent: Keep the idea constant. Change the modality.
steps.visualCaption: The goal is not generation. The goal is audience fit and useful communication.

runbook.openWith: I am keeping the message constant and changing the requested form so we can see what the modality itself does.
runbook.whyMatters: Models the exact comparison students will perform.
runbook.ask: After each version: what improved, what got worse, and what would you verify?
runbook.listenFor: Precision, memorability, simplification, clutter, invented interface details, accessibility, tone.
runbook.ifTheySay: This one looks best → ask whether it teaches best for this audience.
runbook.ifQuiet: Use the second-lock metaphor for MFA and ask what each modality preserves or flattens.
runbook.pushFurther: Which version grabs attention best? Which explains best? Are they the same?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: If the tool fails, that is useful evidence. We test rather than assume.
runbook.landHere: A strong remix preserves the important idea while deliberately changing the experience for the audience.
runbook.transition: Now you will choose who you are designing for before you generate anything.
runbook.say: Prompt: “Explain why multifactor authentication matters to someone who is tired of hearing about cybersecurity.” Keep the core prompt constant while requesting text, an image concept, an audio script, and a short video/storyboard.
runbook.askNext: Which version would you actually use, and why?
runbook.watchFor: Students being impressed by novelty instead of utility.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask which version creates the highest verification burden.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can identify at least one gain and one loss from changing modality.

steps.label: AUDIENCE
steps.title: Who are you designing for?
choices: SOCIAL MEDIA SCROLLER — reason to stop
steps.studentTask: Choose one audience or name your own. Write one sentence: “This person needs ___ from the message.”
steps.roomInstruction: WHO IS THIS FOR? · WHAT DO THEY NEED?
steps.visualCaption: A modality choice is only meaningful relative to a person, purpose, and context.

runbook.openWith: Before you ask AI to make anything, decide who has to understand or act on it.
runbook.whyMatters: Prevents arbitrary modality choices and supports audience-centered reasoning.
runbook.ask: What does your chosen person need from the message?
runbook.listenFor: Clarity, urgency, evidence, low jargon, precision, accessibility, relevance.
runbook.ifQuiet: Offer fun options: roommate, skeptical professor, parent/guardian, student who skipped orientation.
runbook.pushFurther: If you choose an expert audience, what higher verification burden are you accepting?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Audience choice changes what counts as useful.
runbook.landHere: Best modality is always shorthand for best modality for this audience and purpose.
runbook.transition: Now build two genuinely different forms of the same idea.
runbook.studentDoes: Selects a target audience and states its need.
runbook.askNext: Which two modalities give you the most useful comparison for this audience?
runbook.watchFor: Choosing audience after seeing the output.
runbook.advanceWhen: Every student/pair has one audience and one stated need.

steps.label: CREATE
steps.title: AI Remix Challenge
steps.lead: One idea. Two modalities. One audience. Save an artifact.
steps.studentTask: Take ONE idea and communicate it in TWO genuinely different modalities for your audience. Compare what changed. Before time is up, make one human revision to the stronger version and save the before/after evidence.
steps.roomInstruction: ONE IDEA · TWO MODALITIES · ONE AUDIENCE · SAVE AN ARTIFACT
steps.visualAccent: Make the modality choice intentional—not just different.
steps.visualCaption: Public or invented content only. No private or sensitive information.

runbook.openWith: This is not a contest to generate the prettiest thing. I want a comparison you can explain.
runbook.whyMatters: Produces direct evidence for Journal #2: prompts, outputs, audience reasoning, comparison, and human revision.
runbook.ask: Who is this for? Why these two modalities? What became easier? What got lost? What did you change yourself?
runbook.pause: 15 minutes total. Midpoint at ~7 minutes; 3-minute warning for human revision.
runbook.listenFor: Audience fit, purpose, tradeoffs, accessibility, verification, meaningful revision.
runbook.ifTheySay: We are stuck fighting the generator → allow a rough storyboard or switch modality. Reasoning is the target.
runbook.ifQuiet: Idea starters: office hours, sleep before an exam, campus club meeting, phishing, roommate quiet hours, registration deadline, backing up a laptop.
runbook.pushFurther: What is this output making your audience assume? What would you verify before public use?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Privacy rule: use public, invented, or non-sensitive material. Do not upload private messages, grades, health information, passwords, classmate faces, or anything you would not want outside the classroom.
runbook.landHere: The evidence is not just what AI produced. It is what changed, what you noticed, and what you fixed.
runbook.transition: Pick the artifact that gives you the best story about what changed. We are going to compare reasoning, not art.
runbook.studentDoes: Creates two modalities, compares them, revises one, and saves evidence.
runbook.askNext: Which version worked better for your audience—and what evidence in the output supports that?
runbook.watchFor: Two outputs with no audience rationale or no human revision.
runbook.ifStuck: Use the same message, change only the medium.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students/pairs have two versions, one comparison, and one human change.

steps.label: SHOWDOWN
steps.title: The Multimodal Showdown
steps.studentTask: As classmates share, evaluate the reasoning. For each artifact ask: Who was the audience? Which modality worked better? What evidence supports that? What did the human fix or decide?
steps.roomInstruction: MOST USEFUL · BEST AUDIENCE FIT · MOST POLISHED / MOST WRONG · BEST HUMAN SAVE

runbook.openWith: We are not voting on who made the coolest image. We are looking for evidence of good decisions.
runbook.whyMatters: Turns student artifacts into shared evidence and makes failures productive.
runbook.ask: Who was your audience? Which modality worked better? What in the outputs makes you say that? What did the human have to fix?
runbook.listenFor: Specific output evidence, audience reasoning, error detection, revision, verification.
runbook.ifTheySay: This one wins because it looks professional → ask whether it is accurate and useful.
runbook.ifQuiet: Invite one example that failed in an interesting way.
runbook.pushFurther: Could the most polished artifact also be the most dangerous if it is wrong?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Polished-but-wrong is funny at low stakes. It is not funny when money, grades, health, safety, or reputation are involved.
runbook.landHere: Good multimodal work is demonstrated by reasoning and responsible human intervention.
runbook.transition: Let’s make the reliability lesson explicit.
runbook.studentDoes: Compares peer artifacts using audience fit, usefulness, accuracy, and human judgment.
runbook.askNext: What would you verify before sharing or acting on a polished output?
runbook.ifStuck: Use one of the four showdown categories to frame the next share.
runbook.advanceWhen: At least three artifacts have been evaluated with reasons.

steps.label: HUMAN JUDGMENT
steps.title: Polished ≠ accurate.
steps.lead: A beautiful output can still be wrong.
steps.studentTask: Choose the checks that apply to one artifact from today. Then complete: “The AI could generate ___, but a human still needed to ___.”
steps.roomInstruction: VERIFY · EDIT · CHOOSE AUDIENCE · CHECK ACCURACY · ADD CONTEXT · MAKE ETHICAL CALLS
steps.visualAccent: The tool can generate options. You still own the consequence.
steps.visualCaption: Verification should rise with the consequence of being wrong.

runbook.openWith: Realistic-looking is not the same as real. Professional-looking is not the same as trustworthy.
runbook.whyMatters: Directly reinforces SLO 3 and responsible-use judgment after students have experienced the problem.
runbook.ask: What did you personally have to do that AI did not reliably do for you?
runbook.listenFor: Verify facts, remove invented details, add context, revise tone, add alt text/captions, check attribution, decide whether to use the output at all.
runbook.ifTheySay: It looked right → ask what evidence confirmed it.
runbook.ifQuiet: Examples: wrong tutoring-center location, invented 87% statistic, fake campus building, wrong syllabus requirement.
runbook.pushFurther: How much checking is enough for a meme versus financial-aid, health, safety, or academic-policy information?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: The tool accepting an input does not mean you should give it that input. The tool producing an output does not mean you should use it.
runbook.landHere: Human judgment includes verification, context, accessibility, ownership, and consequence.
runbook.transition: Finish by deciding what lesson from today is durable even when the tools change.
runbook.studentDoes: Applies reliability and responsibility checks to a real class artifact.
runbook.askNext: What matters more than finding the 'best' AI tool?
runbook.watchFor: Treating verification as a generic disclaimer.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What would you check before submitting, posting, or acting on this?
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can name one specific human responsibility tied to an artifact.

steps.label: EXIT PULSE
steps.title: What matters more: the “best” AI tool—or the right modality for the audience?
steps.lead: Defend your answer with evidence from something you created or saw today.
steps.studentTask: Respond with evidence, then add: ONE SURPRISE — what worked better than expected? ONE LIMITATION — what did AI get wrong or flatten? ONE HUMAN MOVE — what did you have to decide, edit, or verify?
steps.visualCaption: Save one prompt, one output, one revision, and your reasoning for Journal #2.

runbook.openWith: I want one claim you can defend with evidence from today—not a favorite tool.
runbook.whyMatters: Makes learning visible and collects evidence of transfer beyond a specific product.
runbook.ask: What matters more: the best tool or the right modality for the audience? What from today proves your answer?
runbook.ifTheySay: Video is best because TikTok is popular → ask: for which audience and purpose, and what evidence from today supports that?
runbook.ifQuiet: Use the three prompts: surprise, limitation, human move.
runbook.pushFurther: Which artifact best proves your claim?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: The skill is not memorizing every AI tool. Tools will change. The durable skill is deciding what kind of communication the situation needs—and knowing when not to trust the first thing AI gives you.
runbook.landHere: Choose the modality deliberately. Verify based on consequence. Keep the human decision visible.
runbook.studentDoes: Writes an evidence-based exit reflection and saves journal-ready evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Use the stem: My ___ version worked better for ___ because ___. I still had to ___.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students have submitted the exit pulse.
